preamble: The voiceless retroflex stop /ʈ/ becomes voiced [ɖ] between vowels. This is the usual outcome in languages with retroflex consonants: in Tamil it is regular allophony of a single intervocalic stop, and in Middle Indo-Aryan intervocalic Sanskrit -ṭ- became -ḍ-.

examples.note: A single intervocalic ʈ is voiced to [ɖ] (or flapped [ɽ]); the geminate in பாட்டு pāṭṭu [pɑːʈːɯ] 'song' stays voiceless.
Continued in Gujarati kaḍvũ, Marathi kaḍū and Hindi kaṛvā.
